sections.heading: 1. Book it at the right time
lines: ① Book after a long run or on an easy day.
② Leave 1–2 days before speed work or long runs.
③ Tell your therapist which week you're in.
④ Keep calf and quad strength work going.

sections.heading: 2. See a physio instead if…

a niggle changes your stride — get assessed.

caption:
Toto's marathon block is underway, with long runs every weekend. A deep massage the day before a long run left the legs heavier, not lighter.

Many runners find massage helps tight calves and quads feel looser as the kilometres climb. It's a useful extra, but sleep, food, strength work and a sensible build do most of the recovery.

Timing matters: lighter work after long runs or on easy days, and a day or two of space before key sessions. Tell your remedial massage therapist where you are in your block. Bone pain that builds or a niggle that changes your stride is worth a physio assessment.

Book online via the link in bio.
